newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two hurt in bomb attack on Corsica gendarmes.
newsitem.headline: Two hurt in bomb attack on Corsica gendarmes.

text.p: A bomb exploded near a gendarmerie barracks in Corsica on Friday, slightly injuring a gendarme and a woman, police said.

The attackers also sprayed machinegun fire at the barracks, at Ghinosaccia. It was the first time injuries have been reported in a recent spate of separatist guerrilla attacks at gendarmerie targets on the French Mediterranean island.

The attack bore the hallmarks of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, which has claimed responsibility for seven bomb or machinegun attacks on the holiday island this week.
The FLNC, which has also carried out bombings on the French mainland recently, has threatened new forms of attack and warned families of gendarmes on the island to go home to France.
The latest attack followed the arrest of Corsica's best-known separatist leader Francois Santoni who was remanded in custody in Paris on Wednesday.
Santoni, head of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing, and his lawyer girlfriend Marie-Helene Mattei were placed under investigation for attempted extortion and bomb attacks.
